data.name: Cecelia
data.long_meaning: From the Latin cælea, meaning ‘blind’ or ‘hidden.’ In Christian tradition, the name Cecelia is associated with Saint Cecelia, a third-century martyr. According to legend, she was a wealthy Roman noblewoman who was secretly a Christian and was discovered when she sang to God in her garden. She was persecuted for her faith and endured multiple attempts on her life, but miraculously survived each one. Eventually, she was beheaded, but her body was found to be unharmed three days later. Her feast day is celebrated on November 22.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes hidden faith and inner strength.

data.cultural_impact: Cecelia's name has been a popular one in various European cultures, particularly in Italy and Spain, and it continues to be used in the English-speaking world. The name's association with Saint Cecelia has led to her being revered as the patron saint of music, musicians, and poets. Many musical compositions, including pieces by Gluck, Cherubini, Nahum Tate, and Mendelssohn, have been dedicated to her.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Cecelia carries deep spiritual significance, as it is a reminder of the hidden and often overlooked qualities of our faith. Like Saint Cecelia, who concealed her Christian beliefs from the world, the name suggests the importance of keeping our faith close to our hearts and living it out in hidden, quiet ways. It also serves as a reminder of the power and resilience of the human spirit, even in the face of persecution and adversity. As Saint Cecelia's miraculous survival attests, the strength of our faith can sustain us in the most challenging of circumstances.
